scope: One disposable Supabase Postgres container from the pinned image, two environment databases, the scheduler runner and process on this host; not a running installation.

checks.check: the plpgsql schedule check and the TypeScript parser agree on every schedule in the corpus
cron.schedule by name inserts once, replaces by name, and records the developer as user
an invalid schedule is refused with pg_cron's message, at the function and at the table
scheduling into another database or as another user is refused
alter_job and unschedule work on the caller's own jobs and say so for others
the 101st job is refused
anon, authenticated and service_role reach net.http_* but no role reaches cron without the grant
net.http_post keeps pg_net's Content-Type rule and encodes params as curl does
history older than 7 days and responses older than 6 hours are pruned, and newer ones kept
a run lost by an earlier scheduler is marked failed with "server restarted"
a job runs as the developer, with its search path, and records succeeded with the command tag and its backend
a job that runs RESET ROLE falls back to the scheduler login and gains nothing
a command runs as one simple query, several statements together, and records the last tag
VACUUM alone works, as with pg_cron
a run that ignores its own timeout is ended at the deadline by the scheduler and its backend is gone
a job is never run twice at once
a job whose schedule changes while it runs keeps running on the new schedule
a run is ended at its deadline even while it keeps the bookkeeping session failing
a job streaming hundreds of millions of small rows is ended at its deadline and never holds up the process's event loop
a job streaming COPY TO STDOUT is refused with "COPY not supported", as pg_cron records it, and its backend ends
a job returning 1 GB of rows never holds it: the process peaks below the result's size and is back within 128 MiB once collected, and "50 rows" is recorded
requests to loopback, metadata, private, the database's own address and other schemes are refused, and a public one is answered
a scheduler login password rewritten with 20 million SCRAM iterations does not stall the scheduler process
a queued POST reaches the server with its body, headers and parameters, and the answer is recorded by request id
a job holding the scheduler login's role row does not hold up turning off, turning on or a start
a job that locks the scheduler login out of new sign-ins is still ended at its deadline
a job that locks the scheduler login out and ends its other sessions is still ended at its deadline, as the superuser
without a developer role every run says so and nothing else happens
the scheduler process runs the jobs of an environment endpoints.json lists
a write pause recorded for the environment stops its runs
on SIGTERM the scheduler ends the run in flight and records it
turning off closes the login, takes back its grants and keeps the jobs; a dump then names no such role
turning on again resets the role settings a job wrote for the login and opens it
an archive of the environment, planned as an in-place restore plans it, restores into a stage database of another name with its jobs
a developer session holding the database row (a no-op GRANT left open) does not hold up the connection limit a turn writes beyond its bound
a job holding the developer role row does not hold up a write pause, which ends the scheduler login first
a job holding the database row or the realtime schema row does not hold up turning Realtime on beyond its bound
a second run of the schema SQL changes nothing and keeps the jobs
a developer transaction holding every lock on the schemas' tables does not hold up the schema SQL and grants run again
